Chapter 9: The HP Way in a Changing World
You know, the world never really sits still, does it? Markets shift, technology keeps moving forward, and every new generation brings a fresh perspective—new ideas, new expectations. For HP, that meant facing a big challenge: how do you hold on to what makes you unique, while still keeping up with everything that’s changing around you?
There was a time when HP hit a real crossroads. Suddenly, new competitors were popping up everywhere, and the old ways of doing business just weren’t a guarantee anymore. Some people at HP pushed for big, bold changes. Others wanted to stick with tradition. The debates got pretty lively—sometimes even heated—but there was always respect at the heart of those conversations. And in the end, HP didn’t have to give up its values to move forward. Instead, they found a way to reimagine those values for a whole new era.
The HP Way—those unwritten rules built on trust, respect, and integrity—turned out to be surprisingly strong. They became the company’s compass, guiding tough decisions when the road ahead wasn’t always clear. Sure, HP launched new products and entered markets they’d never been in before, but their core stayed the same: put people first, do what’s right, and keep learning, no matter what.
Of course, it wasn’t all smooth sailing. There were some missteps. Not every experiment turned into a win, and not every choice was popular. But here’s something to pay attention to: HP’s willingness to listen, to admit mistakes, and to try again—that’s what kept them moving forward. Most folks don’t realize just how much strength there is in humility, or how much real innovation comes from being open to change.
As HP grew into a global company, the challenge got even bigger—how do you keep that special culture alive across different continents and time zones? It took some creativity: finding new ways to connect, tell stories, and celebrate wins together. It wasn’t always easy, but the effort made a real difference. The HP Way became more than just a set of practices—it grew into a shared identity, something that united people all around the world.
Looking back, one thing is crystal clear: being able to adapt without losing your soul? That’s rare. Most organizations struggle with change, but the ones that stick to their values—they find a way not just to survive, but to thrive. So, here’s the key takeaway: roots really do matter, but so does growth.
